title: How the Disability Compensation Combined Rating Is Rounded
content:
The combined rating that places a Disability Compensation award on a tier is derived from the VA combined ratings table. Two figures, identical at every tier from Disability Compensation (10% Combined Rating) through Disability Compensation (100% Combined Rating), govern its construction:

- **Bilateral factor: 10 percent.** For disabilities of paired extremities, 10 percent of their combined value is added before they are combined with the other disabilities.
- **Rounding step: 10 percent.** The combined value from the table is rounded to the nearest multiple of 10, and a value ending in 5 is rounded up.

**Rounding illustrations (hypothetical combined values)**

| Combined value from the table | Combined rating | Tier carried |
|---|---|---|
| 44 | 40 | Disability Compensation (40% Combined Rating) |
| 45 | 50 | Disability Compensation (50% Combined Rating) |
| 46 | 50 | Disability Compensation (50% Combined Rating) |
| 94 | 90 | Disability Compensation (90% Combined Rating) |
| 95 | 100 | Disability Compensation (100% Combined Rating) |

**Bilateral illustration (hypothetical).** Where disabilities of both knees combine to a value of 30, the bilateral factor adds 10 percent of 30, that is 3, giving 33 before that value is combined with the veteran's other disabilities.
